newsitem.title: AFGHANISTAN: Afghan opposition warns Taleban to quit town.
newsitem.headline: Afghan opposition warns Taleban to quit town.

text.p: Ousted Afghan government's military chief Ahmad Shah Masood sent an ultimatum to Taleban Islamic forces in the northern town of Kunduz on Thursday to leave the area or face war.

"Our groups are stationed close to Kunduz and if the Taleban and their allies don't leave the area... then we will be forced to take it by military means," Masood's spokesman, Dr Abdullah, told reporters in Kabul by telephone.

He said Masood, who controls forces loyal to ousted president Burhanuddin Rabbani, could not tolerate Taleban's presence in Kunduz, which fell to the purist Islamic militia last week when a local commander, Arif Khan, switched sides.
Abdullah said talks were under way with Khan to persuade him to either surrender the Taleban fighters, who had come to Kunduz from Baghlan province in the south, or evacuate them.

He reiterated opposition alliance's conditions for peace talks with the Taleban, which controls two-thirds of the country, including the capital Kabul they captured from pro-Rabbani forces last September.

"We have a four-point peace plan for talks and solving the problems of Afghanistan -- demilitarisation of Kabul, formation of a broad-based interim government, elections and Kabul as venue of talks," he said.
